text:
Sam: heads up — ran a baseline onboarding job for the new judge pair (ref-embed-3 + ref-judge-2) and the tiebreaker logic looks off

Emily: what do you mean by "off"?

Sam: loads of ties flagged even when humans prefer model A. numbers look fine up to runner, suspect sampling in the harness or our tie heuristics

Raj: can you paste the eval-run command you used?

Sam: `./runner --suite=judge-pairing --seed=42 --sample-mode=prefix-only --quantize=8bit`

Marta: ah — sample-mode=prefix-only is the legacy path. we switched to balanced-sample in the harness last month. if the runner fell back to prefix-only it'll bias short-context prompts.

Nora: CI shows a flaky test that I blamed on docker image changes, but there was a failing job around 2041234000 that altered sampling behavior. look: 
```
[2024-11-03T13:20:11Z] runner:init sampling_mode=prefix-only
[2024-11-03T13:20:11Z] runner:warning override config: sample_mode unset -> defaulting to prefix-only
[2024-11-03T13:20:11Z] harness:loaded tiebreak_policy=majority+randomize
```

Alex: randomize in tiebreak_policy + prefix-only sampling = more ties because truncated context loses disambiguating info.

Emily: is this a config drift or a code regression?

Nora: looks like a small regression in the CI artifact generation step — config schema v2 added `sampling_preference` but the deploy script didn't copy it into the runner config. CI bot artifact still contained old keys.

ci-bot: test/runner-integration #118 failed — missing key `sampling_preference` in artifact (see logs) :warning:

Raj: we should add a guard in the harness that refuses to run judge-pairing without explicit sampling_preference when tiebreaker=majority+randomize. quick patch idea: validate config at startup and bail with an actionable error.

Marta: agreed. also we need a reproducibility note for onboarding docs — new models should run paired with both sampling modes to check sensitivity. put into checklist: `--sample-mode=balanced-sample` and `--sample-mode=prefix-only` and compare tie rate delta.

Sam: on the metric side, tie_rate alone is noisy. propose adding `tie_shift` = fraction of ties that flip in favor of model A when switching sampling mode. helps detect sampling-induced ties.

Emily: nice. can you sketch the math?

Sam: tie_shift = (#cases tied under baseline but modelA wins under alt_mode - #cases tied under baseline but modelB wins under alt_mode) / #tied_baseline. range [-1,1].

Nora: add confidence-weighted variant too (use judge score logits). we'll need to surface both in the dashboard.

Alex: dashboard change request noted — per-pair heatmap with sampling sensitivity column. also show quantization axis because 8bit vs 4bit can amplify ties if logits compress.

Marta: followups: 1) patch harness to validate config (Raj), 2) re-run onboarding job with balanced-sample and seed sweep (Sam + Nora), 3) add tie_shift metric to eval runner (Sam), 4) dashboard PR for sensitivity panel (Alex).

Raj: I'll open a tiny PR for the preflight validation and attach a unit test.

Sam: thanks. will re-run and report numbers. initial manual check suggested tie_rate dropped from 22% -> 6% with balanced-sample for this pair.

Emily: great catch. add the checklist item to the onboarding playbook and mark this a post-merge priority for any judge pair onboarding. :white_check_mark:

Alex: ping me when you have the CSV; I can mock the dashboard tiles locally.

Nora: leaving a note — we should also watch for quantization-specific calibration drift (probability mass reallocation) in the judge models; add eval unit that compares raw logits distribution pre/post-quantize.

Sam: ok thanks all, will post the re-run thread once finished.
